message.content: In Christian tradition, the emphasis is usually placed on Jesus Christ as the central and ultimate figure—often referred to as the “Son of God” and the fulfillment of prophetic expectations. However, many Christians also regard earlier prophets from the Hebrew Scriptures (Old Testament) as significant, such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others, who foretold the coming of the Messiah and shaped the theological foundation of the faith. Different Christian traditions may highlight various prophets or emphasize particular aspects of prophecy, so there isn’t a single universally agreed-upon “most important” prophet beyond the central role traditionally given to Jesus himself.
